body:
Found by queue task 13250 (lane code-v) while landing the #1949 run-seed transport: this property test fails on clean origin/main, unrelated to that change.

## Evidence

- Tree: clean worktree at origin/main 6f1efc4424 (Merge PR #6119), no local changes.
- Command: go test ./internal/testsupport/gen/ -count=1 -run TestConfigLayersProperty in pkgs/mcpx (Go on the laptop, TMPDIR set).
- Result: FAIL — registry_test.go:172: case 0: merged servers = map[alpha:... antigravity:npx beta:... chrome-devtools:npx cloudrun:npx codebase-memory:npx ...], want names [alpha beta delta gamma].
- The merged map contains servers that exist only in the host machine's own MCP configuration (antigravity, chrome-devtools, cloudrun, codebase-memory, context7, deepwiki, fff, gopls-mcp-server, mcp-server-neon, sequential-thinking), which points at the test (or the config layering it exercises) reading real host config instead of only its fixture layers — i.e. the test is not hermetic. On a clean CI runner it may pass; on any developer machine with a populated mcpx config it fails.

## Acceptance

- TestConfigLayersProperty passes on a machine whose real mcpx config names arbitrary extra servers, and still passes in CI.
- The leak path is named in the fix (fixture isolation vs a config-layering bug are different fixes; if layering itself merges host config when it should not, that is the bug and the test caught a real one).

Filed from queue task 13250 bookkeeping; the seed-transport PR references this issue as a pre-existing failure, not a regression.

## Acceptance criteria

- `TestConfigLayersProperty` passes on a developer machine whose host mcpx config contains extra servers: the test exercises only its fixture layers (isolated home/config resolution), never live host configuration.
- A regression case seeds an extra host-style server in the isolated host layer and asserts the merged server names equal the fixture expectation.
- `go test ./internal/testsupport/gen/ -count=1 -run TestConfigLayersProperty` (pkgs/mcpx) is green on the laptop and in CI.
